chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kallub ibn Fiyhas al-Bajali, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Ja'far عليه السلام, that 'Ali عليه السلام used to say:
No judgment is to be passed regarding any of the wounds until it heals.

key_terms.حَتَّى: up to the point that; indicating suspension until a condition is met
key_terms.يُقْضَى: a legal judgment is issued or decided

ai.seo_question: When should judgment be made in cases of wounds and bodily injuries in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal principle concerning bodily injuries: no final judgment is issued regarding wounds until their condition becomes clear through healing. Its significance is in ensuring fairness and accuracy in assessing injury, liability, and compensation.
